_about: The starter dictionary for bendit's controlled vocabulary: one word, one meaning.
Modelled on ASD-STE100, Section 1. This file is DATA. To grow it, run `--init` to copy
it to <repo>/.claude/vocabulary.json and edit the copy; do not edit the script to change
policy. A repo-local file REPLACES this one, so keep the terms you still want.
Rules: `substitute` (exact one-for-one swaps, safe for --fix), `obligation` (a modal
aimed at the agent, instruction files only), `evidence` (a completion claim naming no
observation, report files only). Each term is {"use": replacement, "why": reason}.
Add a term only when you can name what it should say instead, and delete one that
fires more than it catches: a rule that cries wolf gets switched off.
`slop` (advisory, plain writing) is adapted from poteto/noodle's unslop skill (MIT); see `_source`.

substitute._why: ASD-STE100 panel D. Exact one-for-one swaps with no judgment required. Safe to auto-fix.

utilize.why: register inflation; no meaning is added

utilise.why: register inflation; no meaning is added

prior to.why: STE Section 1: BEFORE is the approved form

subsequent to.why: STE Section 1: AFTER is the approved form

commence.why: STE Section 1: START is the approved form

approximately.why: STE Section 1: ABOUT is the approved form

a number of.why: hides whether the count is known

it is imperative that.why: names no actor; STE requires an actor

obligation._why: STE Section 7 requires an unambiguous instruction. A modal addressed to the agent turns a requirement into a suggestion, and the agent takes the suggestion. Only agent-directed modals are flagged; 'a principal that should be denied' describes an expectation and is correct.

should.why: a requirement stated as advice is followed about half the time

try to.why: unfalsifiable: there is no observation that shows it was not tried

where possible.use: name when it is not possible
where possible.why: the agent decides it was not possible

if possible.use: name when it is not possible
if possible.why: the agent decides it was not possible

as appropriate.why: the agent decides what is appropriate

_why: A claim that work is done asserts rung 4 or 5 of the evidence ladder (1 said so, 2 pointed
at the line, 3 showed the bad case cannot happen, 4 ran it and read the output, 5
reproduced it in the running app). This fires when such a claim names no observation: no
rung, no command, no exit code, no file:line, no artifact path, within three lines.
It is aimed at REPORT prose (progress notes, PR bodies, verification writeups), not at
instruction prose, which legitimately discusses these words.

validated.use: name the run and its output

tested.use: name the scenario and the verdict

it works.use: name the run and its output

works as expected.use: name the expectation and the observation

should be fine.use: name what you checked, or say you did not
should be fine.why: a guess stated as a result

looks good.why: a guess stated as a result

successfully.use: delete it, or name the success signal

_why: Plain writing. Phrases and marks that read as machine-written prose, adapted from the unslop list in poteto/noodle.
Advisory only: the report lists them, `--check` and the default run never fail on them, and `--fix` never edits them.
Each entry is a regex `pattern` (case-insensitive, word-bounded unless `raw`), a `use` hint and a `why`.
Code spans, fenced code and tables are not scanned. Patterns that need judgment (rule of three, synonym cycling,
false ranges, colon connectors, title-case headings, bold overuse, missing specifics) are in /bendit:vocabulary, not here.

significance inflation.pattern: pivotal moment|testament to|evolving landscape|setting the stage for|indelible mark|deeply rooted

trailing -ing phrase.use: end the sentence, or give the real source
trailing -ing phrase.why: a participle tacked on to sound significant

vague attribution.pattern: experts (?:believe|say|agree)|industry reports suggest|some critics argue|studies show|observers note
vague attribution.use: name the source, or delete it
vague attribution.why: an unnamed authority cannot be checked

formulaic challenge.use: state the specific problem and what happened

ai vocabulary.use: a plain word: also, important, look into, improve, get, link, detailed, show
ai vocabulary.why: words an assistant uses far more than a person does

copula avoidance.why: a longer way to say is

negative parallelism.pattern: (?:it(?:['’]s| is)|this is|that(?:['’]s| is)) not (?:just|only|merely)\b[^.\n]{0,80}?,\s+(?:it(?:['’]s| is)|but)|not (?:just|merely) [^.\n]{0,60}?,? but\b
negative parallelism.why: 'not X, but Y' argues with a claim nobody made

em dash.use: a period, a comma or parentheses
em dash.why: a common machine-prose tell; prose only, code is not scanned

decorative emoji.why: decoration in a heading or bullet

curly quotes.why: mixed quote styles show a paste from a chat window

chatbot phrase.pattern: i hope this helps|let me know if|of course!|certainly!|great question|happy to help

sycophantic tone.pattern: you(?:['’]re| are) absolutely right|what a great

cutoff disclaimer.pattern: as of my (?:last|knowledge)|while (?:specific )?details are (?:limited|scarce)|limited information is available
cutoff disclaimer.use: find the source, or delete it
cutoff disclaimer.why: a disclaimer in place of a fact

filler phrase.pattern: it(?:['’]s| is) (?:important to note|worth noting) that|needless to say|at the end of the day
filler phrase.use: delete it and start at the point

excessive hedging.pattern: could potentially|might possibly|could possibly|may potentially|it could be argued that

generic conclusion.pattern: the future looks bright|exciting times (?:lie )?ahead|only time will tell|the possibilities are endless
generic conclusion.why: a closing line with no content

inline-header list.use: write it as a sentence, or plain bullets
inline-header list.why: a bolded label that the sentence after it repeats; a label that adds a fact is fine

slop.notice: NOTICE at the repository root carries noodle's full MIT notice for these phrases
slop.note: Adapted, not copied: patterns 1, 3-9, 13, 16, 18-25 of the 25 are matched here; 2, 10-12, 14, 15 and 17 need judgment and are listed in /bendit:vocabulary.
